scope: Read-only diagnosis of Receiving006 operator transition. No acceptance change, source edit, build, live command or network execution.

conclusion.known_trigger: Kubelet restarted the same Pod container for liveness HTTP header timeouts. The previous process handled shutdown and exited0/Completed.
conclusion.unknown_root_cause: Why /healthz missed the1-second deadline is not measured. No direct probe latency/response body, per-process resource series, or goroutine stack was retained.
conclusion.terminal_nats_closure: Not established. Neither terminal closed log literal occurs in the previous log. Do not infer closure from exit0, restartCount+1, or duration of outage.
conclusion.acceptance: Existing operator proof remains failed; these facts do not widen the permitted restart classification.

timeline_utc.event: The inspected operator process starts with the Pod already at restartCount2. Prior startups were unstable; those earlier two restarts precede this proof.
Helper scales only scheduler NATS deployment to0; command exits0.
Previous operator log emits nats disconnected, error EOF.
After observing no scheduler Pod, the150-second outage timer begins.
First recorded liveness header timeout. The aggregated event has count4 and lastTimestamp16:58:37; it is not a per-probe chronology.
Kubelet Killing event: failed liveness probe, will be restarted.
Native manager starts graceful shutdown; controllers receive shutdown signal.
In-flight workload finalizer reports context canceled after shutdown began; this is downstream of the shutdown, not evidence of its cause.
Last retained scheduler-down operator snapshot still reports ready=true and restartCount2. A Kubernetes Ready flag is not a direct contemporaneous HTTP measurement.
Previous process stops caches, webhooks and HTTP server, finishes manager shutdown; lastState shows exit0/Completed at16:58:53.
Helper starts scheduler restoration; the operator shutdown and replacement start already occurred.
Same Pod UID observed with new container ID, restartCount3, ready=false.

native_health_contract.healthz: Ping plus natsLivenessCheck. The latter returns an error only if nc.IsClosed().
native_health_contract.readyz: Ping only; no NATS state call.
native_health_contract.callback_source: runtime-operator/cmd/main.go:196-205 logs disconnect, reconnect and terminal close separately.
native_health_contract.implication: Exhausting a default finite reconnect count cannot be assumed: this helper explicitly reconnects indefinitely. The60-second initial connection window applies only before the first connection, not this already-connected process.

deployed_configuration.chart_note: The chart omits explicit probe timeoutSeconds; observed Kubernetes default is1. There is no operator CPU limit, only a100m request. The192Mi memory limit is real; the observed termination is not OOMKilled.

plausible_confounders_not_findings.hypothesis: NATS-specific health checker latency during reconnect, possibly waiting on client-internal synchronization.
plausible_confounders_not_findings.support: Only /healthz calls IsClosed; readiness stayed true in all sampled snapshots, and unrelated controllers emitted logs during outage. NATS connect timeout5s exceeds probe deadline1s.
plausible_confounders_not_findings.missing: No direct paired health endpoints or client goroutine stacks. The pinned nats.go dependency source was not present in inspected local module caches, so no lock-level causal claim is made.

plausible_confounders_not_findings.hypothesis: Transient process/node scheduling or memory pressure makes a1-second HTTP budget too short.
plausible_confounders_not_findings.support: A low CPU request does not reserve exclusive execution, and these are nested kind nodes sharing a machine.
plausible_confounders_not_findings.missing: No outage-time operator/container CPU, RSS, cgroup pressure/throttle series or node probe-latency series. Pre-proof nodes report no memory/disk/PID pressure, and native host CPU samples near disconnect are around9percent; neither excludes later transient pressure. No CPU cap or OOM cause is established.

plausible_confounders_not_findings.hypothesis: Node-to-Pod transport delay affects the kubelet probe.
plausible_confounders_not_findings.support: Error is deadline while awaiting headers, not a retained negative health response.
plausible_confounders_not_findings.missing: No paired same-node HTTP latency and metrics reachability. Chart NetworkPolicy allows8082 and comments that node-origin kubelet probes are outside its restriction; do not declare a network-policy fault.

plausible_confounders_not_findings.hypothesis: Existing negative workload creates concurrent reconciliation.
plausible_confounders_not_findings.support: flow-http-cross-environment requeues approximately every30seconds throughout the outage; workload-route deletes EndpointSlices at16:57:09 and16:58:09.
plausible_confounders_not_findings.missing: No evidence that this low-rate work consumes the health server or causes the timeout. Preserve it as fixture context, not a cause or a reason to weaken the proof.

rerun_diagnostics.arming: Capture against the exact baseline operator Pod UID and its assigned kind node. Start observational sampling before scale-to-zero, continue through restoration, and retain timestamps, exit/timeout, exact arguments and private raw output. Do not change probes, resources, NATS options or acceptance.

must_capture.purpose: Distinguish NATS-specific health handler delay from whole-process/Pod-path delay. Record body, status, connect time, first-byte time, total time and curl exit for both endpoints within the same sampling interval.
must_capture.cadence: Every5seconds during the existing150-second outage; two requests may run concurrently so a timeout does not serialize the pair.
must_capture.fallback_if_node_curl_unavailable: Record that command failure. Use the existing kubeconfig with kubectl get --raw /api/v1/namespaces/{operator_namespace}/pods/{operator_pod_name}:8082/proxy/{healthz|readyz}, request timeout2s; label it API-proxy-path evidence, not the kubelet path.

must_capture.purpose: Determine whether only the NATS-dependent endpoint stalls and correlate runtime CPU/RSS/GC with the misses.
must_capture.cadence: Before outage, first observed timeout, and before restoration; preserve complete raw metrics privately, publish only selected existing process/Go metric series.
must_capture.limitation: Metrics listen on8081 in the log while chart NetworkPolicy allows the configured service port8443. Node-origin access avoids assuming a new Pod ingress grant; still retain access errors rather than altering policy.

must_capture.purpose: Get per-result probe counter/duration deltas, available kubelet failure timestamps, and operator container resources across the misses. No metrics-server installation is required.
must_capture.cadence: Baseline and first probe timeout, then final; if affordable retain stats/summary every5seconds aligned with paired probes.
must_capture.output_scope: Filter public summaries to the exact Pod UID/container; raw node data stays private. These commands are read-only and need no new RBAC grants in the owned kind fixture.
must_capture.limitation: Kubelet probe metrics are counters/histograms, not individual request traces; ordinary kubelet logs may omit successful probes. Retain endpoint or permission failures without adding grants or changing log verbosity.

must_capture.purpose: Keep the already-added previous/current operator logs, exact Pod/container identities, events and scheduler mutation timestamps. Those established this trigger and must remain.
must_capture.integration: tools/receiving-operator-recovery-run snapshot/continuity and transition diagnostic owners. Retain events after first unhealthy observation as well as after restart, because Event.count/firstTimestamp/lastTimestamp are aggregated.

rerun_diagnostics.remaining_deeper_gap: If paired health confirms only the NATS-dependent endpoint stalls with normal resource/transport measurements, a Go goroutine stack or verified client lock trace is needed to explain it. Current main.go does not configure a pprof endpoint; do not pretend a native stack capture command exists. A terminating SIGQUIT or instrumentation would be separate diagnostic work and cannot count as unchanged-process continuity.

validation: Parsed cited JSON; verified the same Pod/restart delta, clean termination, terminal-close-log absence, liveness Killing event, and resource/probe declarations. No live proof executed.
